question: Is the shape of blast damage falloff between the inner radius and the blast radius stored, and for which explosives?

sourceFacts.method: The six files named BlastCurve_* or *BlastDamageFall* in the saved vehicle and gadget captures were decoded: each holds one curve object (Class_afbfd124) with a list of points (x = Field_3901db14, y = Field_42fc0f5e). The explosion objects (Class_9966532d) of 51 explosive owners were decoded and searched for an import of one of those files; 18 hold one in Field_0839b22b. Every point and each user's own blast damage and radii were re-read at their raw offsets.

control.description: Frag grenade: own InnerBlastRadius 1 / BlastRadius 5 = 0.2, the x of the last full-damage point of its curve. The three vehicle curves are named InnerRadius25, 40 and 50 and start at x = 0.25, 0.4 and 0.5; all end at (0.9, 0.2), EA's 20 percent minimum.

inference: x is distance as a fraction of the blast radius and y is the fraction of blast damage: the frag grenade's own inner radius is 0.2 of its radius and the curve leaves full damage at 0.2; the vehicle curve names give their first x; all three vehicle curves end at 0.2 of damage, EA's stated minimum.

Vehicle shells and missiles with a curve keep full blast damage to 25, 40 or 50 percent of the radius, fall to 20 percent at 90 percent of the radius and stay there. 9 of the 10 owners with a non-zero MinimumBlastDamage row (L3337) import one of these curves.

HEAT-MP-T (MPAT) imports the 25 percent curve: 0.25 x its registry radius 5 = 1.25 m, the lethal radius EA states for 1.3.3.0 (and 0.25 x 4 = 1 m before it). This is the source of EA's 1.25, which the InnerBlastRadius row (1.0) did not give in L3337.

Frag grenade (100 damage, radius 5 m): 100 to 1 m, down to 80 at 3 m, then 60 falling to 40 at 4 m, then 20 out to 5 m. C-4 (radius 3 m): about full to 1.8 m, 80 percent to 2.27 m, about 40 percent to 2.71 m, 20 percent to 3 m. Glaive (radius 4 m): full to 0.5 m, 67 percent to 1.32 m, 33 percent beyond.
Launcher rockets, anti-air missiles, mines, bombs, the 40 mm grenades, the anti-tank grenade and the mortar shell hold no curve import; their falloff shape is not stored in these files.
The distances above use straight lines between points. Each point also stores a mode and tangent values, which were not interpreted; the step points (two x values 0.001 apart) do not depend on them.
unresolved: HEMP-T: the 40 percent curve gives 2.0 m of full damage with radius 5, EA states an inner radius of 2.25 (the registry InnerBlastRadius). Whether the curve or the inner radius sets the full-damage distance when they disagree is not stored. Test: HEMP-T shell landing 2.1 m from a full-health soldier without flak; a kill means the 2.25 radius applies.
Frag grenade steps. Test: grenade exploding 3.5 m from a full-health soldier without flak should deal about 50; at 4.5 m, 20.
Whether a registry radius replaces the own radius when both exist (several of these owners are disputed pairs).
Falloff shape for explosives without a curve (RPG, M136 AT, mines, 40 mm grenades).
siteImpact: None. No Analyzer data, simulation or UI change.

leads.title: Stored blast falloff curves: six curve files give the shape of blast damage with distance for the frag grenade, C-4, the Glaive and vehicle shells
leads.summary: Six stored curve files give blast damage as a fraction of full damage against distance as a fraction of the blast radius. 18 explosion objects import one through Field_0839b22b: the frag grenade, C-4, the Glaive, and the vehicle shells and missiles EA gave a 20 percent minimum (their curves end at 0.2). The 25 percent vehicle curve times the 5 m radius gives EA's HEAT-MP-T lethal radius of 1.25 m. Launcher rockets, mines, bombs and 40 mm grenades have no curve. 106 raw-offset checks matched.
leads.reopenWhen: An in-game blast reading at a measured distance, or a decoded meaning for the point modes and tangents.
leads.statusNote: Curve points and users read; axes named by three value agreements; point modes not interpreted.
